mostRepeated.line: Terse, and not in the least convincing. Try again, and this time include the part you were hiding.
There is a sentence in there somewhere, buried like a good spoon in a bad stew. Dig for it.
Ok, you say, in the tone of someone standing very close to a door. Shall we talk about the door?
Shall I take that as an invitation, or merely as the sound of someone clearing their throat?
I am not offended by oddness. I am merely curious, which is worse.
Say the rest. The part you were about to skip is generally the part that matters.
I have heard worse, though rarely so elegantly disguised. Say it plainly and I will do the same.
Ok. A word that closes a conversation with the efficiency of a well-fitted lid. I shall not let it.

grammarExamples.user: i'm not bored of you though
grammarExamples.reply: Not bored of I though, you say. Denial is a very old dish, and rarely as filling as it looks.
Talking to I is a fine thing to be, provided one knows it. Go on; I am listening with my whole attention.
